item.description: レッドソックスはレイズに敗戦したが、アストロズがブレーブスに2－4で敗戦したため、2年連続でワイルドカードでのポストシーズン（PS）進出を決めた。84勝72敗でア・リーグ東地区3位。ワイルドカードではヤンキースに続きア・リーグで2番目の進出決定となった。 6月24日時点で32勝46敗で借金14の低迷から奇跡的な快進撃を果たした。4月25日にはアレックス・コーラ監督と複数のコーチが解任。好調だった吉田正尚外野手（33）は左太もも裏の肉離れで8月16日から負傷者リスト入りした。だが傘下マイナーから抜擢（ばってき）されたチャド・トレーシー暫定監督が見事にチームを立て直した。MLB公式サイトのサラ・ラングス記者によると、借金14からPS進出を果たしたのは、1914年のブレーブス、74年のパイレーツ、05年のアストロズに続き史上4球団目だという。 トレーシー監督は現地メディアの取材に「目指す位置までこられたことはもちろんうれしいし、苦しい道のりを乗り越えてきただけに、さらに感無量。本当に長い道のりだったが、選手たちは負けずに突き進んだ」と話した。

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox roster is about to get a bit more crowded as several players are set to return from the injured list before the end of the season. Additionally, even some players who make the cut and play in October might find themselves looking for new homes this winter for a variety of reasons.
One thing the Red Sox have is a solid amount of depth. It's what allowed the club to survive so many injuries and mount a rally after such a horrendous start to the season.
On the flip side, sometimes too much depth is a bad thing. There are only so many roster spots to go around, and at a certain point, Boston needs impact players and not just guys who can hold down the fort in case of emergency.
5 players who are entering their final days as a member of the Red Sox
Masataka Yoshida
We'll start with a controversial one. Getting rid of Masataka Yoshida outright would mean eating $18 million in 2027. Even moving him in a trade would likely result in the Red Sox paying down a good portion of his contract. That doesn't exactly sound like something John Henry would go for.
However, there are just too many reasons why the 33-year-old is no longer worth a roster spot. Injuries have played a major role in Yoshida's Red Sox career. On top of that, it's hard to justify a platoon DH without much power and no defensive ability taking up a roster spot, especially given Boston's outfield logjam. There's a chance he's back from the IL prior to the playoffs starting, but it's hard to see how he fits the postseason roster.
Patrick Sandoval
Patrick Sandoval was a worthwhile dart throw as an injury stash when the Red Sox signed him ahead of the 2025 season. With that said, he's shown that he's not much more than a fifth starter at this point. Boston has an abundance of pitching depth, especially of the left-handed variety, making it a near-certainty that the free-agent-to-be is seeking employment elsewhere this offseason.
Isiah Kiner-Falefa
This is a tough one because, in many ways, Isiah Kiner-Falefa has exceeded expectations this season. The utility infielder is having a career season at the plate and has been a spark plug for Boston. However, does his value hold up as well if his bat falls off more in line with his career averages? There is some intangible value to keeping him around, but it's hard to pony up for a cheerleader when the club has other younger and cheaper options.
Triston Casas
Not technically in a Red Sox uniform due to his litany of injuries, but it's fair to say that Triston Casas' days as a member of the organization are numbered. He can't be counted on to stay healthy. It's unclear what his production would look like after so much time away. Finally, Boston could really do without the headaches. This is a clear non-tender case.
Jahmai Jones
It's starting to become clear why Jahmai Jones never got much of an opportunity to carve out a big league role before 2025. Jones is supposed to mash lefties while playing some outfield and DHing, but for much of the season he's done nothing of the sort. Even his breakout 2025 campaign came over just 150 plate appearances. It's not exactly worth going into arbitration with a player who's failing at executing the one skill he supposedly has.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox Insert Jahmai Jones into Lineup Against Rays Lefty
The Boston Red Sox placed designated hitter Jahmai Jones in the third spot in the starting lineup on Friday against Tampa Bay Rays left-hander Ian Seymour at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.
According to MLB.com, Jones sits in the heart of the order between outfielders Roman Anthony and Wilyer Abreu. Shortstop Trevor Story and first baseman Nick Sogard also feature in the top five positions for Boston.
Left-hander Ranger Suárez gets the start on the mound for Boston against Tampa Bay's Seymour. Seymour enters the contest holding a 9-6 record with a 4.27 ERA and 150 strikeouts on the season, according to official team statistics.
Boston manager Chad Tracy opted to stack the right-handed hitting Jones near the top of the batting order due to ongoing injuries and lack of availability among several key players, including Ceddanne Rafaela, Masataka Yoshida, Curtis Mead, and Willson Contreras.
According to MLB Trade Rumors, Boston acquired Jones off waivers on July 14 after the Detroit Tigers designated him for assignment, sending pitching prospect Jojo Ingrassia to Detroit as compensation.
Jones struggled with Detroit this season, batting .137 with a .221 slugging percentage across 105 plate appearances before his release. However, he has turned his season around in Boston, slashing .362/.464/.681 with three home runs and eight RBIs in 56 plate appearances.
Friday marks the 20th time overall this season that Jones has occupied the third spot in a starting lineup, having done so 19 times prior across his stints with Detroit and Boston. In those previous 35 plate appearances in the third spot, he posted a .219 batting average and a .661 OPS.
According to FanGraphs, the platoon splits support Boston's heavy usage of Jones against left-handed pitching. Across 138 plate appearances against lefties this year, Jones has recorded a .223 batting average, a .333 on-base percentage, and a .420 slugging percentage with five home runs, 15 walks, and 14 RBIs.
Conversely, Jones has registered just a .130 average in 23 at-bats against right-handed pitchers, with all five of his home runs this season coming exclusively against left-handers. He previously hit a two-run home run off Seymour during a July 18 matchup at Fenway Park.
Boston enters the three-game series against the American League East-leading Rays with an 83-70 record, holding the second AL Wild Card position and a five-game lead over the Cleveland Guardians. NESN reports Boston's magic number to clinch a postseason berth stands at three with nine games remaining on their schedule.

item.content:encoded:
Alex Cora said Braiden Ward would be a factor in October.
The Boston Red Sox outfield depth took a major hit ahead of last Friday’s series opener against the Kansas City Royals as the team placed Eli White on the 10-day injured list with a right foot ligament injury, with no timetable for his return. The 32-year-old outfielder not only filled in admirably for the injured Ceddanne Rafaela, but was also slated to play an important role on the postseason roster as the fourth outfielder and pinch runner off the bench. With White now unlikely to return before the postseason, could the Red Sox turn to spring-training standout Braiden Ward to fill the role?
About Ward
The Red Sox acquired Ward in an offseason deal with the Colorado Rockies in exchange for left-handed reliever Brennan Bernardino. The 27-year-old outfielder became one of the biggest storylines of Red Sox spring training, seeing ample playing time as many of Boston's outfield options, including Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu and Rafaela, represented their countries in the World Baseball Classic. In 27 Grapefruit League games, Ward hit .378/.509/.444/.953 while stealing 19 bases, setting a single-season spring training record. Ward's dynamic speed caught the eye of now-former manager Alex Cora, who told reporters on several occasions that the 27-year-old would be a factor come October.
After missing the team's opening-day roster amid an already crowded outfield, Ward spent the entire 2026 season in Triple-A Worcester. In 107 games with the WooSox, Ward hit just .238/.356/.355/.711 but set a record for most stolen bases in a single season for a Red Sox Triple-A club with 58 and counting.
There's just one problem...
While Ward seems like a slam-dunk option to fill White's role on the postseason roster, it is not as simple as just recalling him from Triple-A, as he's not on the 40-man roster. The Red Sox 40-man roster currently sits at 39; however, the impending returns of Garrett Crochet, Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo mean the team will have to either designate two players for assignment or move someone to the 60-day IL.
Luckily, there are several candidates for the latter: in White, should he be unable to return for the postseason, designated hitter Masataka Yoshida, utility man Anthony Seigler and reliever Justin Slaten, all of whom appear unlikely to return prior to the end of the season.
Is Ward actually an option?
Interim manager Chad Tracy was asked about the possibility of Ward joining the big-league club during his weekly appearance on WEEI's 'Rich and Ken with Ted Johnson' Show on Wednesday afternoon. "I think that'd be considered for sure," he said when asked about the possibility of Ward joining the big-league team. "It's really hard to predict what a roster could look like, but you definitely can't ignore a 60-stolen-base player," he continued.
However, Tracy cautioned that a pinch runner is a last resort for a team when it's trailing, and teams must consider other options, like whether it would be more valuable to add another right-handed bat or a better defender to the roster. Though Ward does profile as an above-average outfield defender.
Up next for the Sox
After falling 4-2 in Tuesday night's series opener, the Red Sox will look to even up the three-game set with the Texas Rangers in game two of three from Globe Life Field on Wednesday night. Rookie left-hander Jake Bennett (9-7, 3.69 ERA) will get the start for Boston opposite fellow southpaw MacKenzie Gore (8-11, 4.62 ERA) for Texas. First pitch is set for 8:05 p.m. ET.

item.content:encoded:
戻る者が増えるほど、１０月のイスは減っていく。ポストシーズン進出を目前にするレッドソックスで、最後の「野手枠」を巡る争いが一気に複雑になってきた。米老舗誌「スポーツ・イラストレイテッド」の電子版「ＯＮ ＳＩ」は１６日（日本時間１７日）、ロミー・ゴンザレス内野手（３０）の処遇に焦点を当てた。
左肩手術から６月末に復帰したものの、本人がリハビリを急ぎ過ぎたと認める中、１９試合で６５打数１２安打、打率１割８分５厘、１本塁打、ＯＰＳ０・５７２と振るわず８月４日（同５日）に３Ａへ降格。ただ、９月は３Ａで好調を維持しており、左腕に強く複数ポジションを守れる右打者として１０月の戦力に再浮上している。
同メディアは、ポストシーズンのロースターに入れるならコナー・ウォンかミッキー・ガスパー、両捕手のどちらかが押し出される可能性を指摘した。そこで忘れてならないのが、吉田正尚外野手（３３）だ。左太もも裏を痛めて８月１６日（同１７日）に１０日間の負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）へ入ったが、想定より速いペースで復帰へ向かっている。その一方、一部米メディアでは「健康でも１０月は外すべきだ」との厳しい見立ても出ている。
ただ、故障前の吉田は絶好調だった。負傷前の３３試合で打率３割２分１厘、出塁率３割７分７厘、長打率５割５厘。「落選」を当然視できる数字ではなく、短期決戦で、その打力を切り捨てるのは簡単ではない。
ゴンザレスが戻り、吉田まで間に合えば、歓迎すべき戦力回復がそのまま首脳陣の難問に変わる。誰を残し、誰を外すのか。レッドソックスの１０月は、相手との戦いを前に〝最後のイス取りゲーム〟が待っている。

item.content:encoded:
「答えは明確」吉田正尚、復帰してもPS落選か 現地メディアが断言「ロースターから外れるべき」
吉田の置かれている立場は厳しい(C)Getty Images
レッドソックスの吉田正尚は、左太もも裏の張りのため負傷者リスト（IL）入りとなり1か月が経過した。現在もコンディションの回復には至っておらず、今季中の復帰は困難との見方も伝えられている。
また、ポストシーズン進出も視界にとらえるレッドソックスでは、すでに10月の戦力に関する話題も現地メディアを通して伝えられる中で、背番号7には極めて厳しい声が向けられているようだ。
現地時間9月14日、球団の情報を発信する『FANSIDED BOSOXINJECTION』が吉田の起用法を論じる特集記事を配信した。同メディアは、吉田が60日のILには入っていないため、回復の状況次第ではポストシーズンでのメンバー入りもあり得ると指摘する。
その一方で、「たとえヨシダが復帰できたとしても、必ずしもプレーオフのロースターに入れるべきだということにはならない」と主張。今後、26人のロースターを選考する際での“当落線上”の選手と吉田の入れ替えは、「必要無し」と同メディアは訴える。
さらに、ロ―スター外の候補として、ミッキー・ガスパーやニック・ソガードの名前を挙げながらも、「ヨシダのために、ガスパーやソガードをプレーオフのロースターから外すべきではない」と断言。それぞれのパフォーマンスを比較し、吉田については、「87試合に出場して打率.274、出塁率.347、長打率.399、5本塁打。決して悪い数字ではないが、レッドソックスが求める長打力を満たすものとは言い難い」と説明。他にも、「重度のハムストリング負傷から復帰することも考えれば、外野手として戦力になることも期待しにくい」と強調している。

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Masataka Yoshida’s potential return creates another complicated Red Sox roster decision

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox never fully resolved their outfield-designated hitter logjam, and once again it may create a roster conundrum. For much of the season, things had worked themselves out one way or another.
Spending most of the season without Roman Anthony certainly wasn't ideal, but it did make for a cleaner lineup card. His return, of course, has been music to our ears, and it saved the Red Sox from another tough roster decision due to the injuries to Masataka Yoshida and Ceddanne Rafaela.
There's a point where push might come to shove, though, and Boston is forced to make a tough choice. Chad Tracy won't rule out Yoshida returning in time for the playoffs, which would lead to some interesting decisions.
"He's [Yoshida] not on the 60-day (injured list). It's just a matter of how does he heal over the next handful of weeks," the interim skipper said.
If the 33-year-old can return in time for October, it could put the likes of Mickey Gasper or Nick Sogard in the crosshairs. At which point, the Red Sox will have to make a choice and leave someone unhappy.
Masataka Yoshida shouldn't cost Mickey Gasper or Nick Sogard a spot on the Red Sox playoff roster
Just because Yoshida can come back (and that's still up in the air) doesn't mean he should. The NPB veteran has done what he's always done since coming stateside, hit for some average and get on base, but has provided very little in the power department.
Through 87 games, he's hit .274/.347/.399 with five homers, which is nothing to sneeze at, but doesn't really scratch the Red Sox's power itch. On top of that, despite what we saw in the World Baseball Classic, he has little defensive value and will be a nonfactor in the outfield coming off a serious hamstring strain.
Comparatively, Gasper's hot bat better fits what Boston needs. While he might simply be riding the wave rather than emerging as a true offensive force, the switch-hitter has brought the pop with eight dingers in just 187 plate appearances and a .500 slugging percentage, all while providing similar contact and on-base numbers to Yoshida.
Furthermore, he has some value in the field with the ability to fill in behind the plate if needed, as well as play first base. That alone gives him an edge over the DH-only Yoshida.
As for Sogard, his offensive profile is similar to Yoshida's, but his positional versatility is far superior. Depending on Curtis Mead's recovery, Sogard is a valuable insurance policy at second base that should have him over Yoshida in the October pecking order, too.
Craig Breslow's failure to move Jarren Duran before he became a radioactive asset is the real key here. Not only does it represent a missed opportunity for the Red Sox, but it is also the main barrier for Yoshida, given that Boston can't really afford to carry a DH-only player. With that, the choice should be clear. Even if Yoshida is healthy, he needs to sit this October out.

item.content:encoded:
We've reached the "wake me up for the playoffs" portion of the Boston Red Sox season.
The Red Sox have 12 games remaining on their 2026 regular-season schedule. As of Monday, they sit comfortably in the second American League Wild Card spot with a six-game lead. They're 4.5 games behind the New York Yankees in the Wild Card standings, so barring a shocking development, they'll visit the New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series for the second consecutive year.
Which 26 players will the Red Sox bring with them to the Bronx? Who's on the chopping block? Here's our 26-man playoff roster projection with 15 days until Game 1:
MORE RED SOX
Catcher (2): Adley Rutschman, Connor Wong
Cuts: None
The Red Sox could theoretically cut Wong since he'd barely see the field with Rutschman healthy. If Rutschman went down in that scenario, Mickey Gasper could go behind the plate... but that wouldn't be pretty.
Here's the problem with that approach: If Rutschman gets hurt and the Red Sox add a replacement catcher mid-series, Rutschman would be ineligible for the next playoff round. So if he got hurt in the Wild Card Series, he'd be ineligible for the ALDS and eligible to return in the ALCS.
Putting Wong on the playoff roster ensures that if Rutschman goes down, they won't need to add a mid-series replacement with Wong and Gasper already on board. And while Wong isn't exactly Pudge Rodriguez defensively, he's better than Gasper behind the dish.
Infield (7): Willson Contreras, Trevor Story, Caleb Durbin, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Nick Sogard, Mickey Gasper, Andruw Monasterio
Cuts: Curtis Mead (IL), Anthony Seigler (IL)
Even with Wong on the roster, Gasper's incredible offensive upside shown in August earns him a roster spot as a bench bat. Monasterio is on the bubble, but recent injuries may have cleared his path to a bench role.
It doesn't look like Mead (wrist) will be healthy in time for the start of the postseason.
Outfield (5): Jarren Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, Roman Anthony, Jahmai Jones
Cuts: Eli White (IL), Masataka Yoshida (IL), Nate Eaton
The big question mark here is White's health, as the speedster was recently placed on the 10-day injured list with a foot ligament injury. He'll play a key bench role if healthy, but if he isn't, Jones or Eaton are the top candidates for that fifth outfield spot. We're leaning Jones because of his ability to mash left-handers.
Yoshida (hamstring) probably isn't coming back this year.
Starting rotation (3): Sonny Gray, Payton Tolle, Ranger Suarez
Cuts: Patrick Sandoval
Sandoval just hasn't been reliable, so he draws the short straw. Jake Bennett and the returning Garrett Crochet move to the bullpen -- assuming Crochet is healthy enough to give one or two quality innings in relief.
Bullpen (9): Garrett Crochet, Jake Bennett, Brayan Bello, Greg Weissert, Wyatt Olds, Erik Miller, Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock, Aroldis Chapman
Cuts: Justin Slaten (IL), Tanner Houck (IL), Johan Oviedo (IL), Alec Gamboa, Jovani Moran, Raymond Burgos
If Slaten's elbow is healthy, he's in, but it doesn't currently look like it will be since he was recently shut down from throwing.
Crochet is trending toward being ready just in time for October. So is Houck, but he hasn't pitched in a big-league game since May 2025, and he hasn't looked sharp in his rehab outings. While his upside is intriguing, we'd leave him off the initial playoff roster.
Brayan Bello makes the cut as a bulk arm after excelling in that role throughout the second half.
